paragraphs: A Day Behind the Exhibition, posted by Lily. On Saturday morning, the Explorers visited the science museum. Guide Ann showed us the big dinosaur exhibition. The hall was cool, and we stood in a line behind her. The dinosaur was very big. "Nearly eighty people work in this museum," she said. "Each person has an occupation, and today you will meet four of them." Mia took photos. May wrote down the facts.

The first person was an engineer. He keeps the electricity on, and he fixes the machines. "We have twelve engineers in the museum," said Guide Ann. The engineer showed us a small robot with two blue lights. It can move its head and its arms, and children love it. Leo asked, "Can I try?" "Yes," said the engineer, "but you must move the arm slowly." Leo moved the arm, and the robot lifted one hand. Everybody laughed.

The second person was an artist. She painted the big dinosaur model in the middle of the hall. The model is twelve meters long. It is as tall as a house. "It took me three months to paint it," said the artist. She used green, brown, and a little yellow. Lily asked, "Which color was the hardest?" "The brown," said the artist, "because it needs many small lines."

The third person was a writer. He writes the words on every sign in the exhibition. "Each sign has fewer than thirty words," he said, "because visitors do not like long signs." He also writes the quiz for children at the end of the hall. May read the quiz, and she answered all the questions right. The writer smiled. He gave her a small green pencil. The last person worked in the museum shop.

The woman in the shop makes fresh juice every morning. She uses oranges and mango. She makes about thirty glasses. The Explorers each drank a glass of orange juice. Guide Ann said, "Every person here helps the visitors in a different way." Now I know four occupations in a museum. Which occupation do you like best?
